newsitem.title: UK: UK grain futures lower on strong sterling.
newsitem.headline: UK grain futures lower on strong sterling.

text.p: LIFFE wheat and barley futures fell in trading dominated by the effects of sterling's strength.
Once the level of bids was known, the EU's grain export tender had little impact, traders said.

At the current volume of wheat export licences being awarded by the EU grains managment committee, the market would be divided on whether enough was being done to export the available surpluses, they said.
The UK's problem was making itself competitive with other EU origins. "We've got to price ourselves into the market place and I think we're trying to do that at the moment," one trader said.

He felt the low level of farmer selling in the UK was having little effect. Futures traders were basing their thinking on what they felt was likely to happen, and eventually farmers would have to sell the grain they are currently holding.
The most active month in wheat, March, last traded 0.50 stg lower at 94.00 stg, on volume of 221 lots. Total volume was 583 lots.
In barley, active March last traded 0.40 stg lower at 93.50 stg on volume of 32 lots out of a total of 64.
